About

We would rather explain a system than sell one.

Solvanta Energy works with homeowners and businesses on solar, storage and the electrification decisions that follow. Our approach is simple: understand the situation first, design to the data, and write down the assumptions.

Talk to us about your propertyRead our guides

Mission

Make energy decisions that still look sensible in fifteen years.

Australia has some of the best rooftop solar conditions in the world and a fast-moving incentive landscape. Both of those facts make good advice more valuable — and bad advice more expensive.

Our mission is to make the decision legible. That means modelling generation and consumption honestly, explaining where value actually comes from (self-consumption, not feed-in rates), and preparing for changes — an electric vehicle, a heat pump, a battery added in three years.

A system that is designed around your data will outperform a larger system designed around someone else's marketing.

We also believe the customer should be able to audit our work. That is why the estimator on this site shows its assumptions, why our articles link to official sources, and why our incentive information is dated rather than presented as permanent.

How we work

Four commitments we can be held to.

These are not values statements on a wall. Each one shows up in how a proposal is written and how a job is finished.

Accuracy over enthusiasm

If a household's usage does not justify storage, we say so. A smaller, right-sized system that performs is a better outcome than an oversized one that does not.

Assumptions in writing

Every estimate we produce states its inputs: the usage rate, the generation yield, the self-consumption assumption and the incentive treatment. Numbers without assumptions are marketing.

Compliance as standard practice

Safety documentation, network approvals and product eligibility are part of the job, not optional extras. They also protect your ability to claim support you are entitled to.

Respect for the building

Cable routes thought through, roof penetrations sealed properly, equipment placed where it can be serviced. Installation quality is mostly invisible until it fails — so it gets designed in.

Installation philosophy

Good installations are decisions made early.

Almost everything that goes wrong with a solar or battery installation was decided weeks before anyone climbed on the roof.

Specification and sizing detail in any proposal we issue is tied to an assessment of the specific property — not a standard package.

  • Roof, switchboard and shading are checked before a system size is recommended.
  • Generation, self-consumption and export are estimated separately, not bundled into one number.
  • Battery sizing is driven by evening load and surplus, with the capacity taper explained.
  • Backup capability is discussed before installation, because retrofitting it is harder.
  • Monitoring is configured so the system's performance can be checked against the model.
  • Documentation and warranty paths are handed over in writing at completion.

What we will not do

A short list, because it is easier to trust a business that draws its own lines.

  • Quote a savings figure that depends on assumptions we will not disclose.
  • Promise that you will qualify for a government program or a specific rebate value.
  • Present stock photography as a portfolio of our own completed installations.
  • Publish invented statistics, reviews, accreditations or awards.
  • Rush a signature with scarcity tactics or same-day discounts.

Accountability

Who you are dealing with.

A system is designed by someone who has reviewed your consumption data and roof, installed by licensed trades working to the applicable standards, and supported afterwards through the monitoring platform and the warranty paths documented at handover.

Where a proposal includes work by a partner installer, we tell you who is completing it and who holds the responsibility for the workmanship. You should never have to guess who to call.

Estimates, pricing and suitability

How we estimate, and when we advise against buying.

Every number we publish has a listed input, and every recommendation has a reason — including the recommendations not to spend money.

Estimating

Estimates show their inputs, not just their conclusions.

  • Consumption, roof factor, orientation and shading are stated openly rather than buried inside one optimistic headline number.
  • Results are given as ranges — weather, prices and household behaviour move, and a single precise figure would be false precision.
  • Incentive treatment is dated and conditional, because programs change; the treatment applied to any quote is written on the quote.
  • The online estimator is a model with published assumptions. A proposal replaces it with an assessment of your actual property.

Pricing and suitability

Prices map to the work, not to a package.

  • Hardware, mounting, electrical work, cable runs and monitoring are itemised against what the site actually needs.
  • Compliance work — network approvals, safety documentation and program paperwork — is priced as part of the job, not an optional extra.
  • Where site conditions could change the scope, that is flagged before you sign rather than billed as a surprise.
  • Financing is labelled as financing; it is never folded into a headline discount.

The situations where the honest answer is smaller

Storage when there is no evening load to shift. An array sized for exports rather than self-use. Replacing a working inverter on age alone, with no fault and no compatibility reason. If the data does not support the upgrade, we say so — and where it does support it, we show which numbers carry the case.

Independent, and clear about what that means

We are an independent business. We are not a government agency, we do not administer any rebate program, and we cannot determine your eligibility for one. Where we link to official information, we link to the source so you can verify it yourself — including when the news is that a program has closed.
